quiz.title: Inverse Trig Double-Angle Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions on the double-angle inverse-trig formulas and on evaluating a trig function of an inverse-trig value. Choose an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: What is the value of sin(2 tan-1 1/3) + cos(tan-1 2√2)?
The double-angle identity sin(2 tan-1 x) equals which expression?
questions.explanation: Since sin 2A = 2 tanA/(1 + tan²A) and tanA = x when A = tan-1 x, sin(2 tan-1 x) = 2x/(1 + x²).

questions.q: Using a right triangle, what is cos(tan-1 2√2)?
questions.explanation: If tanθ = 2√2, take opposite = 2√2 and adjacent = 1, so hypotenuse = √(1 + 8) = 3. Then cosθ = 1/3.

questions.q: The identity cos(2 tan-1 x) equals which expression?
questions.explanation: cos 2A = (1 - tan²A)/(1 + tan²A), so with tanA = x this gives (1 - x²)/(1 + x²).

questions.q: The identity tan(2 tan-1 x) equals which expression?
questions.explanation: tan 2A = 2 tanA/(1 - tan²A), so with tanA = x this is 2x/(1 - x²).
With tanθ = 3/4, take opposite = 3 and adjacent = 4, so hypotenuse = 5. Then sinθ = 3/5.

faq.q: How do you solve NCERT Exemplar Class 12 Q8 on inverse trig?
faq.a: Split it into two parts. For sin(2 tan-1 1/3) apply the double-angle result 2x/(1 + x²) with x = 1/3 to get 3/5. For cos(tan-1 2√2) draw a right triangle with opposite 2√2 and adjacent 1, giving cos = 1/3. Adding, 3/5 + 1/3 = 14/15.

faq.q: Why does sin(2 tan-1 x) equal 2x/(1 + x²)?
faq.a: Let A = tan-1 x, so tanA = x. The standard double-angle identity sin 2A = 2 tanA/(1 + tan²A) turns straight into 2x/(1 + x²) once you substitute tanA = x. The same idea gives the cos and tan double-angle forms.

faq.q: When should I use the triangle method instead of a formula?
faq.a: Use a right triangle whenever you need a single trig function of one inverse-trig value, such as cos(tan-1 2√2). Label the sides from the given ratio, find the third side by Pythagoras, then read off the function you want. Formulas are faster when a double angle like 2 tan-1 x is involved.

faq.q: What is the final answer and does the order of the two terms matter?
faq.a: The final value is 14/15. Addition is commutative, so it does not matter which term you compute first; sin(2 tan-1 1/3) + cos(tan-1 2√2) and cos(tan-1 2√2) + sin(2 tan-1 1/3) give the same 14/15.
